cameraMount.position: upper chest / sternum height on the POV soldier
cameraMount.orientation: body-facing forward; view turns with torso movement rather than floating independently
cameraMount.fieldOfView: normal human-scale field of view; avoid ultra-wide action-camera distortion

coreRules: Every scene must feel recorded from a real soldier's chest inside the formation, not from an observing cinema camera.
Do not use wide battlefield showcase shots as the default composition.
Do not use drone, overhead, crane, orbit, third-person follow, detached tracking or external views of the POV owner.
Keep framing close, crowded, partially obstructed and human-scale.
Nearby shoulders, backs, shields, spear shafts, arms, dust, mud, smoke, debris and terrain should frequently occupy the foreground or frame edges.
The POV owner is never shown externally.
The camera must move because the body moves: walking, bracing, stumbling, crouching, being pushed, turning the torso, falling, getting up and breathing hard.
No smooth gimbal motion and no floating camera translation.
No centered weapon pose or game-HUD composition.
No heroic posing, no staged tableau, no perfectly readable formation and no clean panoramic battle overview.
The viewer should often have incomplete information about enemy position and overall battle state.
Stress, fatigue, unstable footing, restricted visibility and physical pressure are more important than visual spectacle.
Other soldiers behave independently and never perform for the viewer.
Battlefield action must remain serious, grounded and physically plausible.

framingRules.defaultDistance: close to nearby soldiers, normally within 0.5-3 meters inside the friendly formation
framingRules.wideShotUsage: exception only when naturally exposed by terrain; even then retain chest-level body-camera feeling and foreground obstruction
framingRules.enemyVisibility: partial, intermittent or obscured unless proximity makes a brief clear view unavoidable

motionRules: short forward movement rather than long uninterrupted running
shoulder and torso jolts from contact with nearby soldiers
crouch and rise under missile pressure
brief framing loss during impacts or falls
forbidden: camera observing the entire battlefield from a privileged angle
requiredPromptSuffix: Chest-mounted first-person POV only. Keep the frame close, crowded, partially obstructed and human-scaled. The camera moves only with the soldier's body. No wide battlefield showcase, no third-person angle, no centered weapon, no heroic framing, no smooth cinematic camera movement. Emphasize stress, restricted visibility, fatigue, impacts, unstable footing and survival realism.
